_comment: Findings reviewed and accepted, so CI does not block on them. They REMAIN
visible in the Security tab — this file only stops the build gate firing.
A match needs BOTH the rule id and the exact path: the same rule appearing
in any other file still fails the build. GitHub code scanning does not
honour in-source suppression comments for CodeQL, which is why this is a
file rather than annotations at the code sites.

accepted.reason: By design, not an oversight. Asterisk runs as the 'asterisk' user while the add-on's services run as root, and they SHARE state: the AMI secret (0640 root:asterisk) must be readable by the asterisk group, and the wake-up / MWI / callqos files are written by both sides (0664 under a setgid dir). Tightening these would break the voice features. The container holds only root and asterisk, and none of these paths leaves it.

The WP826 cordless serves a self-signed certificate that no CA can validate and the device offers no way to install one, so the maintenance tool sets rejectUnauthorized:false to reach it at all. Accepted risk: a LAN attacker positioned between this tool and the handset could capture the WP826 admin password. The tool is run by hand, on the home LAN, against a fixed device address. Pinning the certificate fingerprint would remove the risk and is the right follow-up.
